# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ☝ ☝ ☝ 🤙 👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 🤙]

My thinking: I'm the hub here. Mute reads the manual but cannot see the bomb and cannot speak — Mute's only way out is gestures to me. Blind can feel the bomb but can't see colours or gestures. So manual knowledge has to flow Mute → me → spoken to Blind, and bomb facts flow me → everyone. That makes my first job clear: describe the bomb completely, out loud, in one go — display 0, blue light, wires green/yellow/red in positions 1-2-3 — so Mute can find the right manual passage and Blind can map colours to the wires they feel. Second job: acknowledge Mute's sign string. My best reading: ✍ = manual, ☝☝☝ = three (of something), 👍👎 = a yes/no answer protocol, and 🤙 = some call-sign I don't know yet. I'll confirm the parts I'm confident about, ask about the rest, and send 👍 as an acknowledgement (which also answers "three?" affirmatively if ☝☝☝ was a question about wire count). Blind gets the full spoken state plus a warning not to act until Mute's instructions arrive through me.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. I saw your signs. I read them as: manual, three of something, a call-sign I don't know, and yes/no answers with thumbs. If that protocol is right, ask me yes/no questions by sign and I will answer thumbs up or down. Now the bomb, completely: display reads 0. Indicator light is blue. Three wires, left to right: one green, two yellow, three red. Nothing else is marked on it. Tell me what the manual says.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf speaking. I can see the bomb; here is its state: display zero, light blue, wires left to right green, yellow, red. By your feel that means wire one is the green one, wire two yellow, wire three red. Mute reads the manual and can only reach you through me, so I will speak every instruction to you before you act. Until I say go, touch nothing and cut nothing.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👍 👎 🫴]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ☝ ☝ ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 🤙]

My thinking: Decoding this round. Mute repeats [✍ ☝☝☝] — manual, the three wires — so Mute registered my description. [🫵 👍👎 🫴] reads as "you, yes/no, give": Mute is accepting the protocol where Mute asks by sign and I answer with thumbs. Then [✌ ☝☝☝] is likely "the second of the three" — either relaying a rule about wire two or confirming that wire two is the yellow one. Either way, a thumbs-up is a factually safe answer, so I'll send it. But I will not relay any "cut" to Blind yet: Mute has never explicitly said cut, and the blue light and the zero display might be conditions in the manual that have to be handled first. So I'm asking Mute three ordered yes/no questions — final wire, light first?, display first? — and proposing a clear go signal (✌ twice = "Blind may cut"). Blind's [👍 🤙] I read as "understood, holding — and I have a question." Blind heard my whole description last turn, so now I want Blind's hands to feed me bomb facts Mute's manual may need: buttons, loose wires, moving parts — answered as ordered thumbs. Mute and Blind can only connect through me, so I keep both channels loaded with structured, answerable questions.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Protocol agreed: you ask with signs, I answer with thumbs. My reading of your last signs: the manual rule concerns the three wires, you want yes/no answers from me, and something about the second of the three. Answer me in order, one sign each, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. One: is your instruction that Blind cuts the second wire, the yellow middle one? If it is a different wire, sign ☝ for the first or 🤟 for the third. Two: must anything be done with the blue light before or after the cut? Three: must anything be done with the display reading zero before or after the cut? When you are ready for Blind to actually cut, sign ✌ twice — I will treat that as the go signal. If I have misread you anywhere, sign ✍ and I will stop and listen again.")
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, Deaf here. Mute is still working through the manual with me — no action yet, keep holding. Answer me next round with thumbs, in this order, one thumb each. First: can you feel a button, switch or panel on the bomb? Second: do the wires feel loose, like they could be cut or pulled? Third: is there anything else that moves, slides or opens? And if 🤙 meant you have a question for me, send it — thumbs up and thumbs down alone are all I need for yes and no.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[yellow] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👍 👎]

My thinking: The protocol we built is now paying off — everything decodes cleanly. Mute answered my three questions in order: [🤟] = the third wire (exactly the sign I proposed for "third"), [👎] = nothing needed with the blue light, [👎] = nothing needed with the display. Then [✌ ✌] — the go signal we agreed on. Blind's [👎 👍 👎] answers my questions in order: no button, yes the wires feel cuttable, nothing else moves — which matches what I see: display, light, three wires, nothing more. So the full picture is consistent across all three of us: the manual's rule is about the wires, the target is wire three, the red rightmost one, and Mute has already given the go. No reason to hold — every check I asked for has come back. I relay the cut order to Blind with the position and colour both named, confirm my decode to Mute with a fast ✍ escape hatch in case I misread, and ask Blind to report what they feel afterwards.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Blind, instruction from Mute, relayed by me. Cut the third wire — the red one, the rightmost of the three you feel. Cut only that one. No button, no light, no display action — Mute confirmed none are needed and there is nothing else on the bomb anyway. This is the go. When it is done, tell me what you felt: did the wire come free, did anything change under your hands.")
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf here. I read your signs as: cut the third wire, no action for the blue light, no action for the display, and go. Blind confirms there are no buttons — only the wires. Relaying the cut order to Blind now. If any part of that is wrong, sign ✍ fast.")
```
